column2: Duan Qirui Expelled!
column5: ¡Duan Qirui es destituido!

column2: After Yuan Shikai's death, Li Yuanhong became the President and Duan Qirui became the Premier. The Provisional Constitution was reinstated and the parliament convened. However, Li Yuanhong and Duan Qirui had many conflicts, the most glaring of which was over China's entry into World War I. Since the outbreak of the war, China had remained neutral until the United States urged all neutral countries to join the Allies, as a condemnation of Germany's use of unrestricted submarine warfare. Premier Duan Qirui was particularly interested in joining the Allies, because he would then use the opportunity to secure loans from Japan to build up his Anhui Clique army. The two factions in the parliament engaged in ugly debates regarding the entry of China and, in May 1917, Li Yuanhong dismissed Duan Qirui from his government.
column5: Las agrias discrepancias sobre la entrada de China en la Gran Guerra concluyen con la destitución del primer ministro Duan Qirui.

column2: Anhui Threatens Rebellion!

column5: El presidente Li Yuanhong recurre al general monárquico Zhang Xun para mediar en la disputa armada con las provincias rebeldes.

column2: The Qing Restoration
column5: La Restauración Qing

column2: On the morning of July 1, 1917, the royalist general Zhang Xun took advantage of the Anhui affair's chaos, entered the capital, and proclaimed at 4 am, with a small entourage, the restoration of Pu Yi, who had abdicated the throne on February 12, 1912. The capital police submitted the new government. It later published an edict of restoration that falsified the approval of the president of the republic, Li Yuanhong, to general dismay.
column5: Aprovechando el vacío de poder, el general Zhang Xun entra en Pekín y proclama por la fuerza la restauración de Puyi y de la dinastía Qing.

column2: Duan Qirui Reinstated
column5: Duan Qirui es restituido

column2: Over the next 48 hours, edicts by monarchists were proclaimed trying to shore the legitimacy of the restoration. As these edicts included falsified statements by president Li, he fled the presidential palace with two of his aides anticipating hostile actions from the public. He first fled to the French embassy and later stayed in the Japanese embassy. Before taking refuge in the Japanese embassy, Li appointed Vice President Feng Guozhang as acting president and restored Duan Qirui as prime minister to defend the republic. Duan immediately took command of the troops stationed in nearby Tianjin. On July 5, 1917 his troops approached the Beijing-Tianjin railway which was 40 kilometers from the capital. Zhang left the capital to meet Republicans, bolstered by a number of Manchu troops, the same day. With almost all of the Northern Army to oppose him and the Republicans having taken control of the 2 main rail lines to the capital, Zhang was forced to retreat.
column5: Duan Qirui asume el mando de las divisiones de Beiyang en Tianjin y corta las líneas férreas hacia Pekín, forzando la retirada monárquica.

column2: Faced with widespread opposition, Yuan repeatedly delayed the accession rites to appease his foes, but his prestige was irreparably damaged, and province after province continued to declare their autonomy from Beijing. column5: Hubei se separa de la tutela de Pekín, incorporando sus divisiones a la ofensiva republicana.

column2: Guizhou Declares Independence!
column5: ¡Guizhou declara su independencia!

column2: Today, the governor of Guizhou province declared independence from central authority in Beijing. He has agreed to join our cause in overthrowing the central government!
column5: El gobernador de Guizhou rompe vínculos con Pekín y suma sus regimientos al bando de Yunnan.

column2: Sichuan Declares Independence!
column5: ¡Sichuan declara su independencia!

column2: Today, the governor of Sichuan province declared independence from central authority in Beijing. He has agreed to join our cause in overthrowing the central government!
column5: La gobernación de Sichuan rechaza las órdenes del norte y se declara en rebeldía contra Pekín.

column2: Anhui Demands
column5: Exigencias de Anhui

column2: Seeing the weakness of the central government, Duan Qirui and other members of the Anhui Clique demanded greater power in the crumbling Great Chinese Empire or else they threatened to rebel along with the National Protection Alliance.
column5: Duan Qirui y los generales de Anhui exigen el control absoluto del gabinete imperial bajo amenaza de sublevarse con los republicanos.

column2: Government Denounced
column5: El gobierno es denunciado

column2: Sun Zhongshan, the founder of the Republic, has denounced our president Yuan Shikai as having betrayed the Republic and has called for active resistance to our regime.
column5: Sun Yat-sen condena a Yuan Shikai por traición al orden republicano e insta al pueblo a organizar una resistencia armada contra el gobierno.

column2: Demand Repatriation of Sun Zhongshan
column5: Exigir la repatriación de Sun Yat-sen

column2: When President Yuan Shikai took over the fledgling Republic of China, its ideological founder Sun Zhongshan fled to Japan. Given that he is fanning the flames of dissent abroad, should we demand his return?
column5: Exiliado en Japón, Sun Yat-sen coordina la oposición contra Pekín. Las autoridades debaten exigir a Tokio su inmediata repatriación.

column2: Repatriation of Sun Zhongshan
column5: Repatriación de Sun Yat-sen

column2: When President Yuan Shikai took over the fledgling Republic of China, its ideological founder Sun Zhongshan fled to Japan. As a Pan-Asia and republican proponent, Sun Zhongshan was given considerable support by the foreign ministry which hoped his influence would put China firmly in Japan's Sphere of Influence. If his planned rebellion were to be successful, it will create a government much more favorable toward us. If the hypothetical third revolution were to fail, however, it will be better for us to have given in to Yuan's demands for his return instead.
column5: Tokio evalúa respaldar a Sun Yat-sen para afianzar la influencia japonesa en el continente o entregarlo a Yuan Shikai para evitar tensiones diplomáticas.

column2: Trial of Sun Zhongshan
column5: Juicio de Sun Yat-sen

column2: Japan has agreed to handover the insurrectionist Sun Zhongshan. After a short deliberation, the executive council has ordered his execution.
column5: Japón entrega a Sun Yat-sen a las autoridades centrales, un tribunal de Pekín decreta sumariamente su condena y ejecución.

column2: Economic Dominance in China
column5: Hegemonía comercial en China

column2: In the early 1900s, Japan sought to become recognized as a rising Great Power. One of their early priorities was to increase their influence in the splintered Chinese factions. As a result of heavy political lobbying and industrial investment, Japan managed to slowly gain control of the Chinese market, which was good for the home economy.
column5: Inversiones financieras e influencia política aseguran la penetración comercial japonesa sobre los principales mercados del territorio chino.

column2: The Rise of Pan-Asia Sentiment
column5: Auge del panasiatismo

column2: Japanese Pan-Asianism developed in an era when nearby Asian nations were consistently suffering from Western expansionism. Pan-Asian thought in Japan began to develop in the late 19th century and was spurred on particularly following the defeat of Russia in the Russo-Japanese War. Proponents such as Tokichi Tarui and Kentaro Oi attempted to promote a Japanese-Korean defense agreement while others supported anti-western revolutionaries in China and Philippine. In the 20th century however, strong ultra-nationalist tendencies in Japanese society slowly changed the meaning of Pan-Asianism toward supporting aggressive expansion and Japanese imperialism, justified as promoting the unification of Asia under Japan against Western civilization.
column5: El pensamiento panasiático evoluciona en Japón desde una propuesta solidaria anticolonial hacia una doctrina militarista de hegemonía continental.

column2: Let us go forward together
column5: Avancemos en solidaridad conjunta

column2: Japan shall lead the way to a new era of prosperity!
column5: ¡Japón encabezará el liderazgo asiático!

column2: Business Lobby Protests War
column5: Los empresarios protestan contra el conflicto

column2: Due to our economic dominance in China, a group of business leaders who own factories in China have approached the government urging a quick end to the current 'incident' between our two nations before it becomes a full scale war. They fear their assets will be seized by the Chinese government if war is not averted.
column5: Empresarios con intereses en factorías chinas instan a Tokio a detener la escalada bélica para evitar la incautación de sus inversiones.

column2: Make 21 Demands
column5: Exigir las 21 Demandas

column2: Issue a revised 13 Demands
column5: Exigir una versión moderada de 13 Demandas

column2: Unhappiness over Twenty One Demands
column5: Indignación por las Veintiuna Demandas

column2: A coalition of leftist and rightist politicians have united in a rare show of unity to promote unrest within our country. They have used the 21 demands as a rallying point as proof of the Beijing government's betrayal of the people.
column5: Políticos y asambleas estudiantiles condenan la aceptación del ultimátum japonés, calificándolo de sumisión vergonzosa de Pekín.

column2: End of the Second Revolution
column5: Fin de la Segunda Revolución

column2: The KMT's Second Revolution was quickly crushed by forces loyal to the central government. Most of Sun Yat-sen's followers fled to Japan.
column5: La Segunda Revolución del KMT fue aplastada rápidamente por fuerzas leales al gobierno central. La mayoría de seguidores de Sun Yat-sen huyeron a Japón.

column2: Lack of International Recognition
column5: Falta de reconocimiento internacional

column2: Due to our fragile grip on the country, many Western governments refuse to recognize us as the sole authority in China.
column5: Dada nuestra frágil autoridad en el país, muchos gobiernos occidentales se niegan a reconocernos como la única autoridad legítima en China.

column2: Chinese Revolutionary Party
column5: Partido Revolucionario Chino

column2: In July 1914, Sun Yat-sen reorganized Nationalist survivors overseas into the new Chinese Revolutionary Party to oppose the central government.
column5: En julio de 1914, Sun Yat-sen reorganizó a los nacionalistas exiliados en el nuevo Partido Revolucionario Chino para oponerse al gobierno central.

column2: The young Republic of China ordered cruisers and destroyers from Austro-Hungarian shipyards in 1912-1913, but wartime seizures and financial crises halted all delivery.
column5: En 1912-1913 China encargo destructores y cruceros en astilleros austrohungaros, pero la guerra europea y la quiebra fiscal impidieron su entrega.

column2: Too expensive... Build only the cruisers
column5: Demasiado costoso... Comisionar solo cruceros

column2: Too expensive... Build only the destroyers
column5: Demasiado costoso... Comisionar solo destructores

column2: China ordered destroyers from Italy in 1911, but the Italian Navy requisitioned the prototype during the Italo-Turkish War and the remaining hulls were cancelled in 1914.
column5: China contrato destructores a astilleros italianos en 1911, pero la marina italiana incauto el prototipo durante la guerra con Turquia y el resto se cancelo.

column2: Protests erupt in China over concessions awarded to the victorious Great War powers. Should we apply diplomatic pressure for a peaceful resolution?
column5: Estallan protestas en China por las concesiones otorgadas a los vencedores de la Gran Guerra. ¿Debemos presionar diplomáticamente para buscar una resolución pacífica?

column2: Economic Sanctions against Japan
column5: Sanciones económicas contra Japón

column2: Japan has rejected our diplomatic solution to the China problem. Economic sanctions might force them to reconsider.
column5: Japón ha rechazado nuestra solución diplomática al problema chino. Imponer sanciones económicas podría hacerles recapacitar.

column2: Economic Sanctions against Central Powers
column5: Sanciones económicas contra Potencias Centrales

column2: The Central Powers rejected our diplomatic solution for China. Economic sanctions might force a change of heart.
column5: Las Potencias Centrales rechazaron nuestra solución diplomática para China. Unas sanciones económicas podrían hacerles recapacitar.

column2: Beiyang Joins the Triple Entente
column5: Beiyang se une a la Triple Entente

column2: The Beiyang Parliament has joined the Triple Entente. Should we support this, ignore it, or seek Central Powers support to overthrow them?
column5: El parlamento de Beiyang se ha unido a la Triple Entente. ¿Debemos apoyarlo, ignorarlo o buscar el apoyo de las Potencias Centrales para derrocarlos?

column2: Secret Sino-German Pact
column5: Pacto secreto sino-alemán

column2: The rival Chinese government offers a secret pact: laborers for our war effort and future trade concessions in exchange for technical and military aid.
column5: El gobierno rival chino ofrece un pacto secreto: obreros para nuestro esfuerzo bélico y futuras concesiones comerciales a cambio de ayuda técnica y militar.

column2: Beiyang Joins the Central Powers
column5: Beiyang se une a las Potencias Centrales

column2: The Beiyang Parliament has joined the Central Powers. Should we support this, ignore it, or seek Triple Entente support to overthrow them?
column5: El parlamento de Beiyang se ha unido a las Potencias Centrales. ¿Debemos apoyarlo, ignorarlo o buscar el apoyo de la Triple Entente para derrocarlos?

column2: Anhui Clique Breaks Coalition Promises
column5: Anhui rompe el pacto de coalición

column2: Following the failed Qing Restoration, the Anhui and Zhili Cliques had an uneasy power sharing agreement in the Beiyang Government. As part of the agreement, representatives from both cliques shared the Head of State and Head of Government. The Anhui Clique has broken this agreement having ousted Head of State Feng Guozhang and replacing him with an Anhui lackey.
column5: La camarilla de Anhui rompe el pacto de coalición al deponer al presidente Feng Guozhang para colocar a un títere afecto a sus intereses.

column2: Secretly Mobilize
column5: Movilización encubierta de Zhili

column2: Tensions between the Anhui and Zhili factions developed during the Constitutional Protection War of 1917. Duan Qirui, leader of the Anhui clique, favored aggressive military action against the South. The Zhili clique favored compromise and negotiations, hoping to sway rival warlords to their side with financial and political support. Duan refused to acknowledge the Zhili's efforts and favored his own officers and politicians over others. The Anhui Clique has stated they plan to eliminate the various factions in China. Given the breakdown of the Anhui-Zhili coalition, perhaps we should begin mobilization of our forces to protect ourselves.
column5: Ante los planes de Duan Qirui de someter militarmente a las facciones, la camarilla de Zhili procede a la movilización preventiva de sus divisiones.

column2: Rumors of Revolt
column5: Rumores de rebelión

column2: Our intelligence agency has reported an unknown clique is currently planning to form a revolt against the central government.
column5: Informes de inteligencia detectan movimientos conspirativos de una facción militar para sublevarse contra el gobierno de Pekín.

column2: Secretly Agitate Against the Anhui Leadership
column5: Agitación secreta contra Anhui

column2: Having mobilized our army, we should now turn toward seeking diplomatic solutions to curb Anhui Clique's aggressive policies. We can begin by actively opposing the Anhui Clique in the Beiyang Parliament and carefully observing other groups who are sympathetic to our cause.
column5: Con el ejército en alerta, Zhili inicia maniobras de obstrucción política en el parlamento para frenar a Duan Qirui y captar nuevos aliados.

column2: Zhili Clique Discontent
column5: Descontento de la camarilla de Zhili

column2: Our coalition party, the Zhili Clique, is in full revolt in the Beiyang Parliament They have introduced a vote of no confidence against us! This vote is sure to fail, given the implicit threat of forces loyal to us in the Beiyang Army stated to 'protect' the legislators. Still, allowing their agitation to continue on will surely hurt us in the long run. What should our response to their discontent be?
column5: La camarilla de Zhili presenta una moción de censura contra Anhui en el parlamento, el mando debe decidir si pacta o impone su autoridad militar.

column2: Find new coalition partners
column5: Buscar nuevos socios de coalición

column2: Prepare for military intervention (Historic)
column5: Preparar la intervención armada (Histórico)

column2: Reaching out to the Fengtian Clique
column5: Acercamiento a la camarilla de Fengtian

column2: After building a de facto private army using the Nishihara Loans, Duan Qirui used it to occupy Outer Mongolia. Feeling threatened, Northeastern China's Fengtian clique might seek an alliance with us.
column5: La ocupación de Mongolia Exterior por las fuerzas de Duan Qirui empuja a la camarilla manchú de Fengtian a negociar una entente con Zhili.

column2: Rough Draft of the National Salvation Allied Army
column5: Pacto del Ejército Aliado de Salvación Nacional

column2: In November 1919 Zhili clique leader Gen. Wu Peifu met with representatives of Tang Jiyao and Lu Rongting at Hengyang, where they signed a treaty entitled 'Rough Draft of the National Salvation Allied Army'. This formed the basis of a true anti-Anhui clique alliance.
column5: Wu Peifu firma en Hengyang un pacto de asistencia mutua con jefes militares sureños, cimentando la alianza armada frente a Duan Qirui.

column2: Reaching out to the Southern Government
column5: Acercamiento al gobierno del sur

column2: The Zhili Clique historically favored peaceful reunification with the Southern Government. Given the Anhui Clique's increasingly belligerence stance toward them, perhaps the Southern Government would be inclined to support us in any future struggle? We should send diplomats to find out.
column5: Partidaria de la reunificación pacífica, la camarilla de Zhili despacha emisarios para sondear la cooperación militar con el gobierno del sur.

column2: Anhui Arrests Zhili Diplomats
column5: Anhui arresta a enviados de Zhili

column2: The group sent to approach the Southern Government has been arrested by officials loyal to the Anhui Clique on their way back. It seems we not know their stance toward us in any future struggle against the Anhui Clique.
column5: Agentes leales a Duan Qirui detienen a los negociadores de Zhili en su retorno, frustrando la coordinación diplomática con el sur.

column2: Reaching out to Neutral Warlords
column5: Sondeo a caudillos neutrales

column2: After allying with the Fengtian Clique, the Zhili Clique began courting warlords in southwestern China who had previously been threatened by Duan's Anhui armies.
column5: Tras cerrar el pacto con Fengtian, los generales de Zhili buscan sumar al bloque a los caudillos neutrales del suroeste.

column2: Evidence of Imminent Rebellion
column5: Indicios de guerra civil inminente

column2: Reports of a Zhili led rebellion is no longer secret and is now publicly known. We must prepare ourselves for the inevitable war!
column5: Las filtraciones sobre la sublevación inminente de la coalición Zhili-Fengtian se confirman, el choque armado es inevitable.

column2: Oust Anhui Control over the Central Army
column5: Destitución del mando militar de Anhui

column2: Xu Shuzheng Ousted
column5: Xu Shuzheng es destituido

column2: Wu Peifu's Gambit
column5: La maniobra de Wu Peifu

column2: On July 17, Wu Peifu personally commanded the Zhili army's western front performing a daring maneuver outflanking the enemy to attack the western zone's Anhui headquarters.
column5: Wu Peifu asume el mando en vanguardia y lanza una ofensiva de flanqueo sobre el cuartel general de Anhui en el sector occidental.

column2: Western Anhui Front Collapses
column5: El frente occidental de Anhui colapsa

column2: On July 17, Wu Peifu personally commanded the Zhili army's western front performing a daring maneuver outflanking the enemy to attack the western zone's Anhui headquarters. He captured the Anhui army's front-line commander-in-chief Qu Tongfeng and many of his officers, including the 1st Division commander. After taking the town of Zhuozhou, Wu pursued the retreating enemy toward Beijing. With the exception of the 15th Division, the remainder of the Anhui army on the western front was annihilated.
column5: Wu Peifu captura al comandante Qu Tongfeng y aniquila al grueso de las divisiones de Anhui en Zhuozhou, avanzando directamente hacia Pekín.

column2: Wu Peifu Captured
column5: Wu Peifu es capturado

column2: On July 17, Wu Peifu personally commanded the Zhili army's western front performing a daring maneuver outflanking the enemy to attack the western zone's Anhui headquarters. Thankfully, this attack was thwarted by our reinforcements and he has been captured. This will surely harm the enemy's morale.
column5: Los refuerzos de Anhui contienen la acometida de flanqueo y capturan al general Wu Peifu, desarticulando el ataque enemigo.

column2: The Zhili Clique has promised to share power in the Beiyang government if we join them in overthrowing the Anhui Clique.
column5: La camarilla de Zhili ofrece cogobernar el ejecutivo central a cambio de intervenir contra las fuerzas de Duan Qirui.

column2: The Fengtian Clique has declared war on us having sensed the weakness of the central government!
column5: ¡Las columnas manchúes de Fengtian intervienen militarmente contra nuestro gobierno y avanzan hacia la capital!

column2: Beijing is Lost!
column5: ¡Pérdida de Pekín!

column2: We have lost our capital city!
column5: ¡Las defensas han caído y las fuerzas enemigas han ocupado la capital de Pekín!

column2: Fengtian Clique Surrenders!
column5: ¡La camarilla de Fengtian capitula!

column2: Political Instability in the Beiyang Administration
column5: Inestabilidad política en la administración Beiyang

column2: Competing military interests and countless cliques plunged the Beiyang administration into considerable turmoil during the warlord era.
column5: Intereses militares contrapuestos e innumerables camarillas sumieron a la administración de Beiyang en un profundo caos durante la Era de los Señores de la Guerra.

column2: Head of State Changes
column5: Cambios en la Jefatura de Estado

column2: Germany has violated Belgian neutrality and ignored the Treaty of London, providing the British Empire with a direct casus belli.
column5: Alemania ha invadido Bélgica violando el Tratado de Londres de 1839, lo que otorga al Imperio británico un casus belli ineludible.

column2: The Dardanelles Expedition Plan
column5: El plan de la expedición a los Dardanelos

column2: The Admiralty proposes forcing the Dardanelles with naval power and amphibious landings to capture Constantinople and knock the Ottomans out of the war.
column5: El Almirantazgo propone forzar los Dardanelos con apoyo aeronaval y desembarcar tropas para tomar Constantinopla y rendir al Imperio otomano.

column2: Operational Goals: Gallipoli
column5: Objetivos operativos: Galípoli

column2: The objective requires seizing and holding the Gallipoli peninsula (Gelibolu) or knocking the Ottoman Empire out of the war by December 1915.
column5: La operación exige tomar y afianzar la península de Galípoli (Gelibolu) o forzar la capitulación otomana antes de diciembre de 1915.

column2: French Support for the Dardanelles
column5: Apoyo francés en los Dardanelos

column2: The British plan to force the Dardanelles requires Allied cooperation. France dispatches infantry detachments and warships to support the landings.
column5: El asalto aliado a los Dardanelos requiere coordinación, Francia aporta divisiones de infantería colonial y buques de guerra a la operación.

column2: Beachhead Established at Cape Helles
column5: Cabeza de playa en el cabo Helles

column2: Allied amphibious troops secure beachheads at Cape Helles, establishing a fortified operational foothold on the Gallipoli peninsula.
column5: Nuestras brigadas de desembarco consolidan cabezas de playa en el cabo Helles, afianzando posiciones clave en la península de Galípoli.

column2: Seize the Port of Thessaloniki?
column5: ¿Ocupar el puerto de Salónica?

column2: Greek Prime Minister Venizelos invites Allied forces to occupy the port of Thessaloniki to support Balkan operations, defying the King's neutrality.
column5: El primer ministro griego Venizelos ofrece a los aliados ocupar Salónica como base logística contra los imperios centrales, desafiando al rey.

column2: Failure of the Dardanelles Campaign
column5: Fracaso de la campaña de los Dardanelos

column2: Entrenched Ottoman defenses have repulsed all amphibious assaults. The Dardanelles campaign has failed and Allied troops must withdraw.
column5: Las fortificaciones otomanas han repelido los asaltos anfibios. La campaña de los Dardanelos ha fracasado y las tropas deben evacuar.

column2: The McMahon-Hussein Correspondence
column5: Correspondencia McMahon-Huséin

column2: British intelligence establishes diplomatic contact with Hussein bin Ali, Sharif of Mecca, seeking an Arab insurrection against Ottoman rule.
column5: La diplomacia británica inicia contactos confidenciales con Huséin ibn Alí, jerife de La Meca, para promover una revuelta árabe contra los turcos.

column2: Pledges for an Arab Kingdom
column5: Promesas para un reino árabe unificado

column2: High Commissioner McMahon promises British support for an independent post-war Arab state in exchange for an armed revolt against the Ottomans.
column5: El comisionado McMahon ofrece respaldar la independencia de un reino árabe unificado a cambio de que las tribus se alcen contra el Imperio otomano.

column2: Dispatch T.E. Lawrence
column5: Misión de T.E. Lawrence

column2: Captain T.E. Lawrence is dispatched to Arabia to advise the Hashemite forces, coordinating guerrilla raids against Ottoman rail lines.
column5: El capitán T.E. Lawrence es enviado a Arabia para asesorar a las tropas hachemitas y coordinar sabotajes contra el ferrocarril de Hejaz.

column2: Military Assistance to Hejaz
column5: Asistencia militar a Hejaz

column2: With desert supply routes secured, we can deliver small arms, gold, and artillery to support the Arab forces of the Hejaz.
column5: Aseguradas las pistas del desierto, podemos despachar munición, cañones de montaña y fondos para pertrechar a las fuerzas de Hejaz.

column2: Renew Supplies to Hejaz
column5: Renovar suministros a Hejaz

column2: The Arab uprising continues to make progress along the Red Sea coast. Continued supply deliveries sustain their momentum toward Damascus.
column5: La rebelión árabe avanza por la costa del mar Rojo, mantener el envío de convoyes artilleros asegura el impulso hacia Damasco.

column2: Loss of Al-Arish
column5: Pérdida de Al-Arish

column2: Ottoman forces have stormed our positions and captured the vital desert outpost of Al-Arish.
column5: Tropas otomanas han desbordado nuestras líneas y capturado la posición de Al-Arish en el Sinaí.

column2: Loss of the Suez Canal
column5: Pérdida del canal de Suez

column2: Enemy forces have seized the Suez Canal, cutting the lifeline between Great Britain and India.
column5: Las fuerzas enemigas han ocupado el canal de Suez, quebrando la arteria marítima entre Gran Bretaña y la India.

column2: Loss of Alexandria
column5: Pérdida de Alejandría

column2: Enemy forces have taken Alexandria, compromising our strategic naval base in Egypt.
column5: Tropas enemigas han capturado Alejandría, comprometiendo la base naval principal en el Mediterráneo oriental.

column2: Loss of Port Sudan
column5: Pérdida de Port Sudan

column2: Enemy spearheads have seized Port Sudan, severing maritime communications along the Red Sea.
column5: Columnas enemigas han tomado Port Sudan, interrumpiendo el tráfico mercante en el mar Rojo.

column2: Loss of Khartoum
column5: Pérdida de Jartum

column2: Enemy forces have entered Khartoum, toppling British military administration across the Sudan.
column5: Fuerzas enemigas han capturado Jartum, desarticulando el control militar británico en Sudán.

column2: Fall of Cairo
column5: Caída de El Cairo

column2: Enemy armies have occupied Cairo, our authority over Egypt has collapsed.
column5: Las divisiones enemigas han entrado en El Cairo, nuestra administración en Egipto ha caído.

column2: Enemy Landing at Dover
column5: Desembarco enemigo en Dover

column2: Enemy amphibious forces have landed at Dover, threatening the British home islands directly.
column5: Fuerzas anfibias enemigas han desembarcado en Dover, el territorio metropolitano británico está amenazado.

column2: Enemy Landing at Norwich
column5: Desembarco enemigo en Norwich

column2: Hostile amphibious troops have seized beachheads near Norwich, invading eastern England.
column5: Tropas de desembarco enemigas han asegurado cabezas de playa cerca de Norwich, invadiendo el este de Inglaterra.

column2: Enemy Landing at Edinburgh
column5: Desembarco enemigo en Edimburgo

column2: Enemy assault troops have landed near Edinburgh, compromising defenses in Scotland.
column5: Fuerzas de asalto enemigas han desembarcado en Edimburgo, comprometiendo la defensa de Escocia.

column2: Enemy Landing at Glasgow
column5: Desembarco enemigo en Glasgow

column2: Hostile forces have executed amphibious landings at Glasgow, cutting communications across Scotland.
column5: Tropas enemigas han tomado posiciones anfibias en Glasgow, amenazando los astilleros del Clyde.

column2: Enemy Landing at Manchester
column5: Desembarco enemigo en Mánchester

column2: Enemy divisions have landed near Manchester, cutting through our industrial heartland.
column5: Divisiones enemigas han desembarcado en el sector de Mánchester, partiendo en dos el territorio insular.

column2: Enemy Landing at Cardiff
column5: Desembarco enemigo en Cardiff

column2: Enemy forces have landed at Cardiff, opening a hostile front in southern Wales.
column5: Fuerzas enemigas han desembarcado en Cardiff, abriendo un frente de invasión en Gales.

column2: Enemy Landing at Plymouth
column5: Desembarco enemigo en Plymouth

column2: Hostile troops have landed at Plymouth, threatening the naval dockyards of Devon.
column5: Tropas enemigas han desembarcado en Plymouth, amenazando los arsenales de Devonshire.

column2: Enemy Landing at Dublin
column5: Desembarco enemigo en Dublín

column2: Enemy expeditionary forces have landed in Dublin, occupying eastern Ireland.
column5: Tropas expedicionarias enemigas han desembarcado en Dublín, ocupando el este de Irlanda.

column2: Enemy Landing at Portsmouth
column5: Desembarco enemigo en Portsmouth

column2: Enemy assault divisions have landed at Portsmouth, threatening our premier naval anchorage.
column5: Divisiones enemigas han asaltado Portsmouth, amenazando la base naval principal del Canal.

column2: Fall of London
column5: Caída de Londres

column2: London has fallen to enemy forces. Government and King have been forced to evacuate.
column5: Londres ha caído ante las columnas enemigas, el gobierno y la corona evacuan la capital.

column2: Secret Russian Consultations on Serbia
column5: Consultas secretas rusas sobre Serbia

column2: Russian envoys request Allied support to safeguard Serbian sovereignty against Austro-Hungarian aggression, aiming to preserve balance in the Balkans.
column5: La diplomacia rusa solicita el respaldo aliado para frenar la coacción austrohúngara sobre Serbia y asegurar los Balcanes.

column2: Naval Blockade of Germany
column5: Bloqueo naval contra Alemania

column2: The Royal Navy deploys distant patrols to cut off maritime commerce to the Central Powers, restricting raw materials and food imports into Germany.
column5: La Royal Navy establece un bloqueo marítimo para asfixiar la economía alemana cortando sus importaciones de ultramar.

column2: German Submarine Counter-Blockade
column5: Bloqueo submarino alemán

column2: German U-boats have begun interdicting British merchant convoys, inflicting tonnage losses that threaten our food and raw material imports.
column5: Los sumergibles alemanes atacan nuestras rutas mercantes, amenazando con estrangular las importaciones de alimentos y metales.

column2: German Unrestricted Submarine Warfare
column5: Guerra submarina irrestricta de Alemania

column2: Germany declares unrestricted submarine warfare, authorizing U-boats to sink all merchant vessels in British approaches without prior warning.
column5: Alemania proclama la guerra submarina sin restricciones, ordenando torpedear sin previo aviso a mercantes en aguas británicas.

column2: Sinking of the RMS Lusitania
column5: Hundimiento del RMS Lusitania

column2: A German U-boat has torpedoed and sunk the liner RMS Lusitania, killing over 120 American citizens and swinging US public sentiment toward the Allies.
column5: El hundimiento del RMS Lusitania por un sumergible alemán causa más de 120 víctimas estadounidenses, inclinando a Washington hacia los Aliados.

column2: Lusitania Munitions Cargo Exposed
column5: Contrabando bélico del Lusitania al descubierto

column2: Berlin proves the Lusitania carried munitions in its hold, dampening American outrage and reinforcing isolationist sentiment in Washington.
column5: Berlín demuestra que el Lusitania transportaba pertrechos de guerra, frenando la indignación pública en Estados Unidos y reforzando a los aislacionistas.

column2: The Zimmermann Telegram Intercepted
column5: Interceptado el telegrama Zimmermann

column2: British codebreakers intercept the Zimmermann Telegram, revealing German offers of an anti-American alliance to Mexico with promises of lost territories.
column5: Los descifradores británicos interceptan el telegrama Zimmermann, donde Berlín ofrece a México recuperar Texas y Arizona si ataca a Estados Unidos.

column2: Alliance Rapprochement with Portugal
column5: Alineamiento diplomático de Portugal

column2: British Request for Portuguese Belligerence
column5: Petición británica de entrada en guerra

column2: Brazil Enters the War
column5: Brasil entra en la guerra

column2: Repeated U-boat sinkings of Brazilian merchant ships such as the Paraná inflame domestic outrage, compelling Brazil to declare war on Germany.
column5: El torpedeamiento de cargueros neutrales como el Paraná desata protestas masivas, forzando a Brasil a declarar la guerra a Alemania.

column2: The Easter Rising in Dublin
column5: El Levantamiento de Pascua en Dublín

column2: Armed republicans under Patrick Pearse and James Connolly seize key buildings in Dublin, proclaiming an independent Irish Republic during Easter week.
column5: Militantes republicanos armados toman edificios en Dublín durante la Pascua de 1916, proclamando la República de Irlanda frente a la corona.

column2: Total Military Collapse
column5: Colapso militar británico

column2: Enemy forces have penetrated the British home islands and broken our defensive lines. The Empire must concede defeat and sign an armistice.
column5: Fuerzas enemigas han ocupado suelo británico y quebrado la defensa nacional. No queda otra opción que capitular y pedir el armisticio.

column2: Armistice with the British Empire
column5: Armisticio con el Imperio británico

column2: The British Empire has concluded an armistice following decisive battlefield defeats. Formal peace negotiations will determine territorial cessions.
column5: El Imperio británico ha firmado el armisticio tras sufrir decisivas derrotas militares, la conferencia de paz fijará las pérdidas coloniales.

column2: Britain Proposes a White Peace
column5: Gran Bretaña propone paz blanca

column2: Great Britain has proposed a white peace, agreeing to restore the status quo ante bellum and consolidate current territorial borders.
column5: Gran Bretaña ofrece una paz blanca sin anexiones para detener las hostilidades y restablecer las fronteras de preguerra.

column2: The Entente Concludes Peace
column5: La Entente firma la paz

column2: Capitulation of Serbia
column5: Capitulación de Serbia

column2: Serbia has signed unconditional surrender. Austro-Hungarian forces occupy and formally annex the Serbian kingdom.
column5: Serbia ha firmado la rendición incondicional, el ejército austrohúngaro procede a la ocupación y anexión del reino.

column2: Capitulation of Montenegro
column5: Capitulación de Montenegro

column2: Montenegro has capitulated. Axis authorities occupy the territory and install a subservient client administration in Cetinje.
column5: Montenegro ha capitulado, las fuerzas de ocupación establecen un gobierno títere subordinado a los intereses de Viena.

column2: Capitulation of Hejaz
column5: Capitulación de Hejaz

column2: Hejaz has capitulated to Ottoman forces, ending Hashemite rebellion across the Arabian peninsula.
column5: El reino de Hejaz ha capitulado ante las fuerzas imperiales, sofocándose la rebelión hachemita en la península arábiga.

column2: Capitulation of Kuwait
column5: Capitulación de Kuwait

column2: Kuwait has capitulated, Ottoman troops occupy the sheikhdom and install a friendly administrative authority.
column5: Kuwait ha capitulado, tropas otomanas ocupan el emirato e instauran un gobierno afín a Estambul.

column2: The End of the German Blockade
column5: El fin del bloqueo alemán

column2: Since we are now at peace with their country, the Germans have lifted their blockade and we can once again trade without restrictions.
column5: Restablecida la paz con Alemania, los alemanes levantan el bloqueo naval y el comercio marítimo se reanuda sin restricciones.

column2: Germany refused to guarantee Swiss neutrality while France agreed, violating the 1815 Treaty of Paris and providing a clear casus belli.
column5: Alemania se nego a garantizar la neutralidad suiza mientras Francia acepto, violando el Tratado de Paris de 1815 y otorgando un casus belli.

column2: Germany declared war on France. The Entente Cordiale does not mandate military intervention, we could choose splendid isolation instead.
column5: Alemania declaro la guerra a Francia. La Entente Cordiale no obliga a intervenir militarmente, podriamos mantener el aislamiento.

column2: Finland's declaration of independence
column5: Declaración de independencia de Finlandia

column2: On December 6, 1917, the Finnish Parliament declared national independence, which was officially recognized by Soviet decrees later that month.
column5: El 6 de diciembre de 1917 el parlamento finlandes proclamo la independencia nacional, reconocida por decretos soviéticos ese mismo mes.

column2: Finland's hard times
column5: Tiempos dificiles en Finlandia

column2: Deep social divisions polarized independent Finland between conservative Whites in the countryside and radical socialist Reds in urban industrial areas.
column5: Profundas divisiones sociales polarizan Finlandia entre los blancos conservadores rurales y los rojos socialistas urbanos.

column2: The recognition of Finland's independence
column5: Reconocimiento de la independencia de Finlandia

column2: Though recognizing Finnish independence, Soviet Russia backed the radical Red Finns with weapons during the subsequent Finnish Civil War.
column5: Aunque reconocio la soberania finlandesa, la Rusia soviética apoyo con armas a los guardias rojos durante la guerra civil.

column2: Soviet Russia declared war upon us!
column5: ¡La Rusia soviética nos declara la guerra!

column2: Soviet Russia refused to accept our sovereignty and declared war. Survival depends on securing German assistance.
column5: La Rusia soviética rechaza nuestra soberania y nos declara la guerra. La supervivencia depende de la ayuda alemana.

column2: Finland wants to join the Central Powers
column5: Finlandia solicita unirse a las Potencias Centrales

column2: Newly independent Finland requests an alliance, offering to establish a monarchy ruled by a German King.
column5: Finlandia solicita ingresar a nuestra alianza, proponiendo instaurar una monarquia bajo la corona de un rey alemán.

column2: Finland joins the Central Powers
column5: Finlandia se une a las Potencias Centrales

column2: Germany accepted our proposals and welcome us in the Central Powers
column5: Alemania acepto nuestras propuestas e integro oficialmente a Finlandia en las Potencias Centrales

column2: Announce Regency
column5: Proclamar la Regencia

column2: While Prince Frederick Charles of Hesse was elected King, ongoing wartime conditions established a temporary regency under Mannerheim.
column5: Aunque se eligio rey a Federico Carlos de Hesse, la guerra impuso una regencia provisional encabezada por Mannerheim.

column2: Germany won the Great War
column5: Alemania vence en la Gran Guerra

column2: Following German victory, preparations are finalized to crown Prince Frederick Charles as King Frederik Kaarle I of Finland.
column5: Con el triunfo alemán en la guerra, todo esta dispuesto para coronar al principe Federico Carlos como rey de Finlandia.

column2: Germany lost the Great War
column5: Alemania pierde la Gran Guerra

column2: Germany's defeat prompted Prince Frederick Charles to renounce the Finnish crown, paving the way for republican presidential elections.
column5: La derrota alemana motivo la renuncia del principe al trono finlandes, abriendo paso a elecciones presidenciales republicanas.

column2: Finnish Civil War
column5: Guerra Civil Finlandesa

column2: The post-Tsarist power vacuum led to civil war in January 1918 between the conservative White Guards and the socialist Red Guards.
column5: El vacio de poder tras la caida zarista desemboco en enero de 1918 en una guerra civil entre la Guardia Blanca y la Guardia Roja.

column2: The Finnish Socialist Workers' Republic
column5: República Socialista Obrera de Finlandia

column2: The Finnish People's Delegation formed a revolutionary Red government in Helsinki, signing an alliance treaty with Lenin's Soviet Russia.
column5: La Delegación Popular formo el gobierno revolucionario rojo en Helsinki, firmando un tratado de alianza con la Rusia soviética.

column2: Support the revolutionaries in Finland?
column5: ¿Apoyar a los revolucionarios finlandeses?

column2: With Finland engulfed in civil war, should Soviet Russia send arms to support the socialist workers' government in Helsinki?
column5: Con Finlandia en plena guerra civil, ¿debe la Rusia soviética enviar armas al gobierno socialista obrero de Helsinki?

column2: Soviet Russia supports us!
column5: ¡La Rusia soviética respalda nuestra causa!

column2: Soviet Russia signed a friendship pact with our revolutionary government, providing shipments of weapons and supplies.
column5: La Rusia soviética firmo un pacto de amistad con nuestro gobierno revolucionario, facilitando envíos de armas y pertrechos.

column2: The conservative Senate and the White Guards have crushed the Red Guard, winning the Finnish Civil War.
column5: El Senado y las fuerzas de la Guardia Blanca han derrotado por completo a la Guardia Roja, ganando la guerra civil.

column2: The Finnish People's Delegation and the Red Guard have triumphed over the White forces, securing socialist control of Finland.
column5: La Delegación Popular y la Guardia Roja han derrotado al bando blanco, consolidando el control socialista sobre Finlandia.

column2: Join Soviet Russia?
column5: ¿Integrarse en la Rusia soviética?

column2: Victorious Red elements propose formal annexation into the Russian SFSR as a constituent Soviet republic.
column5: Tras vencer en la guerra civil, sectores radicales proponen la anexión formal a la RSFS de Rusia como república soviética.

column2: Finland joins Soviet Russia
column5: Finlandia se integra en la Rusia soviética

column2: Following socialist victory, the Finnish People's Delegation petitioned for full union with the Russian SFSR.
column5: Tras el triunfo socialista, la Delegación Popular solicito la incorporación de Finlandia en la RSFS de Rusia.

column2: Ask Germany for support?
column5: ¿Solicitar ayuda a Alemania?

column2: Locked in brutal civil combat with the Red Guards, White forces require urgent military intervention from Germany to prevail.
column5: Enfrascados en una dura guerra civil contra la Guardia Roja, dependemos de la ayuda militar alemana para sobrevivir.

column2: Alliance with the German Empire?
column5: ¿Alianza con el Imperio Alemán?

column2: Following Germany's victory in the Great War, forging an alliance could secure lasting protection for our nation.
column5: Tras la victoria alemana en la Gran Guerra, forjar una alianza garantizaría protección estratégica para nuestra nación.

column2: First Presidential Elections
column5: Primeras elecciones presidenciales

column2: The 1919 Finnish elections pitted liberal reformer K.J. Stahlberg against monarchist general Mannerheim.
column5: Los comicios finlandeses de 1919 enfrentaron al reformista liberal K.J. Stahlberg con el general monarquico Mannerheim.

column2: Elect Stahlberg as President
column5: Elegir a Stahlberg presidente

column2: Elect Mannerheim as President
column5: Elegir a Mannerheim presidente

column2: The Greek Political Dilemma
column5: El dilema político griego

column2: Greece faces the 'National Schism': a pro-German King Konstantinos I opposed by pro-Entente Prime Minister Eleftherios Venizelos.
column5: Grecia afronta el «Cisma Nacional»: el rey Constantino I, de simpatías germanófilas, choca con el primer ministro anglófilo Eleftherios Venizelos.

column2: Bulgaria Enters the War
column5: Bulgaria entra en la guerra

column2: Bulgaria enters the war against Serbia, prompting fresh clashes between King Konstantinos and Venizelos over Greece's treaty duties.
column5: Bulgaria declara la guerra a Serbia, reavivando el choque entre el monarca y Venizelos sobre las obligaciones defensivas de Grecia.

column2: Entente Territorial Guarantees
column5: Oferta territorial de la Entente

column2: The Entente offers territorial gains in Thrace and Asia Minor (the Megali Idea) in exchange for Greek entry into the war.
column5: La Entente ofrece ganancias en Tracia y Asia Menor (la Megali Idea) si Grecia abandona la neutralidad y declara la guerra al Eje.

column2: Entente Alliance Overtures
column5: Propuesta de alianza de la Entente

column2: The Entente proposes an alliance against the Central Powers, but offers no specific guarantees concerning neutral Bulgaria.
column5: La Entente propone una alianza militar, pero omite garantías específicas respecto a las intenciones de la vecina Bulgaria.

column2: King Konstantinos Falls Ill
column5: Enfermedad del rey Constantino

column2: King Konstantinos falls gravely ill with pleurisy, sparking intense rumors and political paralysis in Athens amidst the ongoing European crisis.
column5: El rey Constantino contrae una severa pleuresía, paralizando la corte de Atenas en plena crisis internacional.

column2: Recovery of King Konstantinos
column5: Recuperación del rey Constantino

column2: Following surgical treatment, King Konstantinos recovers and resumes direct political leadership in Athens.
column5: Tras una intervención médica, el rey Constantino se restablece y asume nuevamente la dirección de los asuntos de Estado.

column2: The Dardanelles Crisis in Athens
column5: La crisis de los Dardanelos en Atenas

column2: With the Dardanelles landings underway, Chief of Staff Metaxas opposes Greek intervention while Venizelos insists on joining the Allies.
column5: Ante las operaciones en Galípoli, el coronel Metaxas amenaza con dimitir si Grecia interviene, mientras Venizelos exige unirse a los Aliados.

column2: The Gounaris Initiative
column5: La iniciativa de Gounaris

column2: Prime Minister Gounaris offers Entente entry provided Allied armies guarantee Greek borders against future Bulgarian attacks.
column5: El primer ministro Gounaris ofrece combatir junto a la Entente a condición de que los Aliados blinden la frontera frente a Bulgaria.

column2: 1915 Greek Parliamentary Elections
column5: Elecciones legislativas de Grecia de 1915

column2: Venizelos' Liberal Party wins a decisive parliamentary majority, compelling King Konstantinos to reappoint him Prime Minister.
column5: El Partido Liberal de Venizelos vence en las elecciones, obligando al rey Constantino a llamarlo nuevamente al gobierno.

column2: Order defensive mobilization only
column5: Ordenar solo una movilización defensiva

column2: Allied Forces Land at Thessaloniki
column5: Desembarco aliado en Salónica

column2: Allied troops disembark and occupy the port of Thessaloniki with Venizelos' secret consent, infuriating royalist factions in Athens.
column5: Fuerzas de la Entente desembarcan en Salónica con el beneplácito de Venizelos, profundizando la fractura con los monárquicos.

column2: Allied Demand for Greek Demobilization
column5: La Entente exige la desmovilización griega

column2: The Entente demands the demobilization of the Greek army to eliminate the threat of a royalist strike against their rear at Thessaloniki.
column5: La Entente exige licenciar a las tropas griegas para disipar el riesgo de una ofensiva monárquica contra su retaguardia en Salónica.

column2: Early Parliamentary Elections
column5: Elecciones parlamentarias anticipadas

column2: With political factionalism paralyzing policy, the King considers dissolving parliament to secure an anti-interventionist royalist majority.
column5: Ante el bloqueo político entre el trono y el parlamento, el rey evalúa disolver la cámara para afianzar un gabinete neutralista.

column2: Serbian Troops Land on Corfu
column5: Tropas serbias desembarcan en Corfú

column2: Allied ships evacuate the remnants of the Serbian Army across Albania and land thousands of soldiers on Corfu without Athens' consent.
column5: Buques aliados evacuan los restos del ejército serbio y desembarcan tropas en la isla griega de Corfú sin consultar a Atenas.

column2: Bulgarian Access to Greek Territory?
column5: ¿Paso militar a Bulgaria?

column2: To balance Allied occupation in Macedonia, royalist authorities consider permitting Bulgarian forces to advance into eastern Greek territory.
column5: Para contrarrestar la ocupación aliada en Macedonia, los monárquicos evalúan autorizar el avance búlgaro en el este de Grecia.

column2: Arson at Tatoi Royal Palace
column5: Incendio en el palacio real de Tatoi

column2: A devastating arson fire damages the royal estate at Tatoi, injuring King Konstantinos and killing several guards amidst Allied covert friction.
column5: Un grave incendio intencionado devasta el palacio de Tatoi, hiriendo a Constantino I y matando a miembros de la guardia real.

column2: The National Defense Schism in Thessaloniki
column5: El gobierno rebelde de Salónica

column2: Venizelos proclaims the Provisional Government of National Defense in Thessaloniki, creating an open schism with the royalist government in Athens.
column5: Venizelos proclama el Gobierno de Defensa Nacional en Salónica, consumando la fractura territorial e institucional con la monarquía de Atenas.

column2: Allied Demobilization Ultimatum
column5: Ultimátum de desmovilización de la Entente

column2: The Entente delivers a strict ultimatum demanding Greece demobilize its army to prevent coordinated Axis operations against Thessaloniki.
column5: La Entente presenta un duro ultimátum exigiendo desmovilizar al ejército griego para conjurar la amenaza sobre el frente macedonio.

column2: The Noemvriana Clashes in Athens
column5: Las «Vísperas Griegas» en Atenas

column2: French naval landing detachments arrive in Athens to seize Greek artillery batteries, sparking street confrontations with royalist troops.
column5: Marineros franceses desembarcan en Atenas para incautar baterías costeras, desatando choques armados con reservistas griegos.

column2: Allied Demand for Royal Abdication
column5: Exigencia aliada de abdicación real

column2: The Allies enforce a naval blockade and demand King Konstantinos abdicate in favor of Prince Alexander, clearing the path for Greece to join the war.
column5: La Entente impone un bloqueo naval y exige la abdicación de Constantino I en su hijo Alejandro para sumar a Grecia a sus filas.

column2: Greek Military Collapse
column5: Colapso militar griego

column2: Greek defensive lines have crumbled, enemy forces have overrun the country, forcing an unconditional capitulation.
column5: Las líneas defensivas se han quebrado y las divisiones enemigas ocupan el país, forzando la capitulación incondicional.

column2: The Treaty of Athens: Central Powers Dictate
column5: Tratado de Atenas: Victoria de las Potencias Centrales

column2: The Central Powers dictate peace terms: Greece cedes frontier districts, demobilizes its armed forces, and pays substantial war reparations.
column5: Los imperios centrales imponen el Tratado de Atenas: Grecia cede provincias fronterizas, desarma su ejército y paga reparaciones.

column2: The Treaty of Athens: Entente Dictate
column5: Tratado de Atenas: Victoria de la Entente

column2: The Entente dictates peace terms: Greece surrenders contested provinces, demobilizes standing formations, and pays war reparations.
column5: La Entente dicta los términos de paz: Grecia cede distritos en litigio, desmoviliza sus tropas y asume indemnizaciones de guerra.

column2: Italian Concerns over the July Crisis
column5: Inquietud italiana ante la crisis de julio

column2: Austria-Hungary delivers an ultimatum to Serbia without prior consultation with Rome, straining our obligations under the Triple Alliance.
column5: Austria-Hungría entrega un ultimátum a Serbia sin consultar a Roma, contraviniendo el espíritu consultivo de la Triple Alianza.

column2: The Treaty of London Negotiations
column5: Negociaciones del Tratado de Londres

column2: Britain and France offer Trentino, Trieste, Istria, and parts of Dalmatia if Italy abandons the Triple Alliance and declares war on Austria-Hungary.
column5: Gran Bretaña y Francia ofrecen el Trentino, Trieste, Istria y Dalmacia si Italia rompe la Triple Alianza y declara la guerra a Viena.

column2: Italy Enters the War with the Entente
column5: Italia entra en la guerra con la Entente

column2: Italy formally honors its treaty commitments to the Entente, declaring war on the Austro-Hungarian Empire to reclaim Italia Irredenta.
column5: Italia cumple sus compromisos con la Entente y declara la guerra al Imperio austrohúngaro para conquistar las tierras irredentas.

column2: Loss of Bergamo
column5: Pérdida de Bérgamo

column2: Austro-Hungarian troops have breached our northern lines and captured Bergamo.
column5: Tropas austrohúngaras rompen nuestras líneas del norte y toman Bérgamo.

column2: Loss of Brescia
column5: Pérdida de Brescia

column2: Enemy forces have captured Brescia, opening routes into Lombardy.
column5: Fuerzas enemigas capturan Brescia, abriéndose paso en Lombardía.

column2: Loss of Venice
column5: Pérdida de Venecia

column2: Austrian troops have occupied the historic city of Venice.
column5: Las tropas austríacas han ocupado la ciudad de Venecia.

column2: Loss of Udine
column5: Pérdida de Udine

column2: Enemy forces have captured Udine, outflanking the Isonzo defense sector.
column5: Tropas enemigas capturan Udine, desbordando el dispositivo defensivo del Isonzo.

column2: Loss of Turin
column5: Pérdida de Turín

column2: Enemy armies have occupied the major industrial center of Turin.
column5: Ejércitos enemigos toman Turín, ocupando el principal centro industrial del Piamonte.

column2: Loss of Parma
column5: Pérdida de Parma

column2: Hostile troops have occupied Parma, pushing south of the Po River.
column5: Tropas hostiles entran en Parma, rebasando la línea del río Po.

column2: Loss of Ancona
column5: Pérdida de Ancona

column2: Enemy spearheads have seized the Adriatic port of Ancona.
column5: Vanguardias enemigas aseguran el puerto adriático de Ancona.

column2: Fall of Rome
column5: Caída de Roma

column2: Enemy armies have entered Rome, central government authority has collapsed.
column5: Las divisiones enemigas ocupan Roma, la autoridad del gobierno central se desmorona.

column2: Loss of Naples
column5: Pérdida de Nápoles

column2: Enemy forces have occupied Naples, cutting off southern Italy.
column5: Fuerzas enemigas ocupan Nápoles, aislando el sur de Italia.

column2: Italian Military Collapse
column5: Colapso militar de Italia

column2: Enemy armies have breached the Alpine wall and occupied Rome. With our forces routed, Italy must accept unconditional surrender.
column5: Los ejércitos enemigos han forzado los pasos alpinos y ocupado Roma. Rotos los frentes, no queda más remedio que la rendición incondicional.

column2: Armando Diaz Appointed Chief of Staff
column5: Armando Diaz nombrado Jefe del Estado Mayor

column2: Following the Caporetto disaster, General Armando Diaz replaces Cadorna as Chief of Staff, reorganizing the defense along Monte Grappa and the Piave.
column5: Tras el desastre de Caporetto, el general Armando Diaz releva a Cadorna y reorganiza las defensas en el Monte Grappa y el río Piave.

column2: Japanese Ultimatum to Germany
column5: Ultimátum japonés a Alemania

column2: Invoking the Anglo-Japanese Alliance, Tokyo delivers an ultimatum to Germany demanding the unconditional handover of Tsingtao and naval withdrawal from Asian waters.
column5: Amparándose en la alianza con Gran Bretaña, Tokio envía un ultimátum a Alemania exigiendo la entrega de Tsingtao y la retirada de su flota en Asia.

column2: Demand all German Pacific colonies!
column5: ¡Exigir todas las posesiones alemanas del Pacífico!

column2: German Silence on Japanese Ultimatum
column5: Silencio alemán ante el ultimátum japonés

column2: Germany has ignored our ultimatum regarding Tsingtao and the Pacific. The Empire of Japan must declare war to enforce its demands.
column5: Alemania no ha respondido al ultimátum sobre Tsingtao y el Pacífico. El Imperio de Japón debe declarar la guerra para hacer valer sus exigencias.

column2: Germany Accepts Japanese Demands
column5: Alemania acepta las exigencias de Japón

column2: Germany unexpectedly agrees to transfer its Pacific holdings to preserve Japanese neutrality. We must decide whether to honor our pledge or join the Entente.
column5: Inesperadamente, Alemania acepta ceder sus posesiones del Pacífico a cambio de nuestra neutralidad. Debemos decidir si honramos el pacto o nos unimos a los Aliados.

column2: Japan Offers a White Peace
column5: Japón propone una paz blanca

column2: Japan offers a white peace, confirming current territorial acquisitions and ending naval operations in the Pacific.
column5: Japón ofrece una paz blanca, consolidando las posiciones capturadas y poniendo fin a las hostilidades en Extremo Oriente.

column2: Declare Jihad
column5: Proclamar la Yihad

column2: The Ottomans declared Jihad
column5: Los otomanos proclaman la Yihad

column2: The supporters of Senussi are taking control of the inner provinces
column5: Los sanusies toman el control del interior

column2: Ottoman holy war declarations incited Libyan tribes, forcing Italian troops to abandon Fezzan and Tripolitania except for coastal ports.
column5: La proclamación otomana de guerra santa incito a las tribus libias, forzando a Italia a evacuar el interior y conservar solo plazas costeras.

column2: The Tripolitanian leaders rally to our cause
column5: Caudillos de Tripolitania se unen a la causa

column2: Disparate tribes in Fezzan and Tripolitania fielded tens of thousands of fighters, mounting fierce resistance against Italian forces.
column5: Diversas tribus de Fezzan y Tripolitania alzaron a miles de guerrilleros, presentando una ferrea resistencia contra las guarniciones italianas.

column2: The Senussi are ready to strike
column5: Los sanusies listos para atacar

column2: Request Senussi invasion of Egypt
column5: Solicitar a los sanusies una ofensiva contra Egipto

column2: The Ottomans want us to attack Egypt
column5: Los otomanos solicitan atacar Egipto

column2: The Senussi accepted our proposal
column5: Los sanusies aceptan la propuesta

column2: The Senussi accepted our proposal and started their own invasion of Egypt.
column5: La Orden Sanusi acepto nuestra propuesta e inicio su avance contra Egipto.

column2: Truce with Italy and France
column5: Tregua con Italia y Francia

column2: With France and Italy prioritizing the European front, operations in Libya were restricted to local engagements.
column5: Con Francia e Italia volcadas en el frente europeo, los choques en territorio libio quedaron reducidos a combates locales.

column2: The Senussi are at war with the United Kingdom
column5: Los sanusies en guerra con Gran Bretana

column2: Support from the Germans
column5: Llega el aprovisionamiento alemán

column2: The British defeated us
column5: Derrota frente a los británicos

column2: The Senussi sue for peace
column5: Los sanusies solicitan la paz

column2: Peace with the British
column5: Paz con los británicos

column2: Recognize Idris al-Senussi as Emir of Cyrenaica and Fezzan
